[George Washington](/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington"), the first president of the United States

As the nation's first president, [George Washington](/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington") established many norms that would come to define the office.[[27]](#cite_note-31)[[28]](#cite_note-32) His decision to retire after two terms helped address fears that the nation would devolve into monarchy and established a precedent that would not be broken until 1940 and would eventually be made permanent by the [Twenty-Second Amendment](/wiki/Twenty-Second_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Twenty-Second Amendment to the United States Constitution"). By the end of his presidency, political parties had developed,[[29]](#cite_note-33) with [John Adams](/wiki/John_Adams "John Adams") defeating [Thomas Jefferson](/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") in 1796, the first truly contested presidential election.[[30]](#cite_note-34) After Jefferson defeated Adams in 1800, he along with [James Madison](/wiki/James_Madison "James Madison") and [James Monroe](/wiki/James_Monroe "James Monroe") would each serve two terms, eventually dominating the nation's politics during the [Era of Good Feelings](/wiki/Era_of_Good_Feelings "Era of Good Feelings") until Adams' son [John Quincy Adams](/wiki/John_Quincy_Adams "John Quincy Adams") won election in 1824 after the [Democratic-Republican Party](/wiki/Democratic-Republican_Party "Democratic-Republican Party") split.

The election of [Andrew Jackson](/wiki/Andrew_Jackson "Andrew Jackson") in 1828 was the first time someone outside of the Virginia and Massachusetts elite won

**Visa requirements for Japanese citizens** are administrative entry restrictions by the authorities of other states placed on citizens of [Japan](/wiki/Japan "Japan").

As of 2026, [Japanese citizens](/wiki/Japanese_nationality_law "Japanese nationality law") had visa-free access to 187 countries and territories, ranking the [Japanese passport](/wiki/Japanese_passport "Japanese passport") 2nd in the world according to the [Henley Passport Index](/wiki/Henley_Passport_Index "Henley Passport Index").[[1]](#cite_note-1)

From 2018 to 2022, Japanese citizens had visa-free or visa on arrival access to the most countries and territories,[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2) making the Japanese passport rank first in the world in terms of travel freedom according to the [Henley Passport Index](/wiki/Henley_Passport_Index "Henley Passport Index").[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4) It ranked 2nd in 2023 and 2024.[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2)[[5]](#cite_note-5)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Joe_Biden_81st_birthday.jpg/250px-Joe_Biden_81st_birthday.jpg)](/wiki/File:Joe_Biden_81st_birthday.jpg)

Biden's 81st birthday cake

As of 2025, Biden was the oldest sitting president in U.S. history. His cognitive health was perceived to have declined by Republicans and some media figures,[[680]](#cite_note-701)[[681]](#cite_note-cbsjuly1age-702) and privately by some Democrats. Members of Biden's family and White House staffers insulated Biden from scrutiny of his advanced aging and decline in acuity.[[682]](#cite_note-703)[[683]](#cite_note-wsjagedec-704)[[684]](#cite_note-705)

The media widely covered public concern about Biden's mental acuity after a weak performance in a June 2024 presidential debate,[[681]](#cite_note-cbsjuly1age-702) but gave it limited coverage beforehand, in part due to harsh pushback from White House officials.[[685]](#cite_note-706) Biden initially deemed himself fit to serve two terms as president,[[686]](#cite_note-707) but after the 2024 election said that he may have been too old to serve a second term.[[687]](#cite_note-708)

As part of the [investigation into Biden's handling of classified documents](/wiki/Joe_Biden_classified_documents_incident "Joe Biden classified documents incident"), special counsel [Robert Hur](/wiki/Robert_Hur "Robert Hur") said that Biden did not remember when he was vice president ("if it was 2013—when did I stop being vice president?") or when his son Beau died.[[688]](#cite_note-709) Hur wrote that his memory "appeared to have significant limitations".[[689]](#cite_note-710)

On July 21, 2022, Biden tested positive for [COVID-19](/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") with reportedly mild symptoms.[[690]](#cite_note-711)[[691]](#cite_note-A

The Yangtze has played a major role in the [history](/wiki/History_of_China "History of China"), [culture](/wiki/Culture_of_China "Culture of China"), and [economy of China](/wiki/Economy_of_China "Economy of China"). For thousands of years, the river has been used for water, irrigation, sanitation, transportation, industry, boundary-marking, and war. The [Yangtze Delta](/wiki/Yangtze_Delta "Yangtze Delta") generates as much as 20% of [China's GDP](/wiki/Historical_GDP_of_China "Historical GDP of China"), and the [Three Gorges Dam](/wiki/Three_Gorges_Dam "Three Gorges Dam") on the Yangtze is the [largest hydro-electric power station in the world](/wiki/List_of_largest_hydroelectric_power_stations "List of largest hydroelectric power stations").[[12]](#cite_note-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13) In mid-2014, the Chinese government announced it was building a multi-tier [transport network](/wiki/Transport_network "Transport network"), comprising railways, roads and airports to create a new economic belt alongside the river.[[14]](#cite_note-ChinaEconomy-14)

The Yangtze flows through a wide array of ecosystems and is habitat to several [endemic](/wiki/Endemism "Endemism") and threatened species, including the [Chinese alligator](/wiki/Chinese_alligator "Chinese alligator"), the [narrow-ridged finless porpoise](/wiki/Yangtze_finless_porpoise "Yangtze finless porpoise"), and also was the home of the now extinct [Yangtze river dolphin](/wiki/Yangtze_river_dolphin "Yangtze river dolphin") (or *baiji*) and [Chinese paddlefish](/wiki/Chinese_paddlefish "Chinese paddlefish"), as well as the [Yangtze sturgeon](/wiki/Yangtze_sturgeon "Yangtze sturgeon"), which is [extinct in the wild](/wiki/Extinct_in_the_wild "Extinct in the wild"). Internationally, Google has over 78 offices in more than 50 countries.[[292]](#cite_note-293)

In 2006, Google moved into about 300,000 square feet (27,900 m2) of office space at [111 Eighth Avenue](/wiki/111_Eighth_Avenue "111 Eighth Avenue") in [Manhattan](/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), [New York City](/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"). The office houses its largest advertising sales team.[[293]](#cite_note-294) In 2010, Google bought the building housing the headquarters, in a deal that valued the property at around $1.9 billion.[[294]](#cite_note-295)[[295]](#cite_note-296) In March 2018, Google's parent company Alphabet bought the nearby [Chelsea Market](/wiki/Chelsea_Market "Chelsea Market") building for $2.4 billion. Phelps was chosen to be the [American](/wiki/United_States_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "United States at the 2016 Summer Olympics") [flag bearer](/wiki/List_of_flag_bearers_for_the_United_States_at_the_Olympics "List of flag bearers for the United States at the Olympics") at the [opening ceremony](/wiki/Olympic_Games_ceremony#Opening "Olympic Games ceremony"), which was the first Olympic opening ceremony that he would attend.[[232]](#cite_note-auto1-232)[[233]](#cite_note-233) Phelps was also voted by the U.S. Olympic swim team as one of six [team captains](/wiki/Captain_(sports) "Captain (sports)") for the [US delegation](/wiki/United_States_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "United States at the 2016 Summer Olympics") to the Olympics.[[234]](#cite_note-234) He displayed a relaxed, sociable demeanor in the athletes' village and in press conferences; this pleasant behavior was in stark contrast to his isolation in previous Olympics.[[224]](#cite_note-nbcolympics.com1-224) He was accompanied by fiancée Nicole Johnson and son Boomer.[[235]](#cite_note-235)

In his first event on August 7, the [4 × 100 m freestyle relay](/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_4_%C3%97_100_metre_freestyle_relay "Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay"), he won his first gold medal of the 2016 Games and his 19th Olympic gold medal overall. Phelps swam the second leg with what his coach Bob Bowman described as "maybe the best turn that's ever been done",[[236]](#cite_note-236) overtaking France's [Fabien Gilot](/wiki/Fabien_Gilot "Fabien Gilot") to give his American teammates a lead which they would not relinquish.[[237]](#cite_note-237) Phelps's leg proved to be the decisive factor in the race, and Gilot later remarked "As fast as my teammates were, the extraterrestrial that is Phelps was faster".[[231]](#cite_note-thestar.com-231) Phelp

Mike Ross, a university expellee with a [photographic memory](/wiki/Eidetic_memory "Eidetic memory"), makes money by taking the [LSAT](/wiki/Law_School_Admission_Test "Law School Admission Test") and the [bar examination](/wiki/Bar_examination_in_the_United_States "Bar examination in the United States") for others. He does this to pay for his grandmother's living expenses, as she was his primary caregiver after both his parents died in a car accident when he was 11. In the pilot, Mike agrees to deliver a briefcase of [cannabis](/wiki/Cannabis "Cannabis") for his best friend Trevor, a drug dealer, for a large payout. Mike astutely avoids being arrested in a [sting](/wiki/Sting_operation "Sting operation"), only to stumble into a job interview with Harvey Specter, a supremely self-assured [senior partner](/wiki/Partner_(business_rank) "Partner (business rank)") at the prestigious Pearson Hardman, a law firm specializing in [corporate law](/wiki/Corporate_law "Corporate law") and one that only hires [Harvard](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University") graduates. Harvey is impressed by Mike's tenacity and knowledge of the law and hires him as an [associate](/wiki/Associate_attorney "Associate attorney"), despite Mike's not having a license to practice law.[[13]](#cite_note-14) Together they try cases while maintaining Mike's secret from the rest of the firm, though Harvey's insightful [legal secretary](/wiki/Legal_secretary "Legal secretary"), Donna Paulsen, finds out almost immediately. Mike meets Rachel Zane, an ambitious [paralegal](/wiki/Paralegal "Paralegal") he is immediately attracted to, while trying to impress [managing partner](/wiki/Managing_partner "Managing partner") Jessica Pearson and avoid the suspicions of [junior partner](/wiki/Junior_partner "Junior partner") Louis Litt.

The Steelers have also won eight [AFC championships](/wiki/AFC_Championship_Game "AFC Championship Game"), tied with the [Denver Broncos](/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), but behind the Patriots' record 12 AFC championships. The team is tied with the Broncos, the [Dallas Cowboys](/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys"), and the [San Francisco 49ers](/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers") for the second-most Super Bowl appearances with eight.

When Kennedy ran for president in 1960, one of his key election issues was an alleged "[missile gap](/wiki/Missile_gap "Missile gap")" with the Soviets. In fact the US at that time was ahead of the Soviets and by an increasingly wide margin. The US had 170 ICBMs and was quickly building more. It also had eight [*George Washington*](/wiki/George_Washington-class_submarine "George Washington-class submarine")- and [*Ethan Allen*-class](/wiki/Ethan_Allen-class_submarine "Ethan Allen-class submarine") [ballistic missile submarines](/wiki/Ballistic_missile_submarine "Ballistic missile submarine"), with the capability to launch 16 [Polaris](/wiki/UGM-27_Polaris "UGM-27 Polaris") missiles, each with a range of 2,500 nautical miles (4,600 km). The six [European Cups](/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") Liverpool won from 1977 to 2019 on display in the club's museum

In terms of the number of trophies won, Liverpool is regarded as the [most successful club in English football](/wiki/List_of_football_clubs_in_England_by_competitive_honours_won "List of football clubs in England by competitive honours won"). Liverpool's first trophy was the Lancashire League, which it won in the club's first season.[[4]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKelly198815-4) In 1901, the club won its first League title, while the record-equalling twentieth and most recent was in 2025.[[177]](#cite_note-177) Meanwhile, the club's first success in the FA Cup came in 1965. In the 1980s, Liverpool had its most successful decade, when the club won six League titles, two FA Cups, four League Cups, one Football League Super Cup, five [Charity Shields](/wiki/FA_Community_Shield "FA Community Shield") (one shared) and two European Cups. In 2020, Liverpool became the first English club to have won a League title in eight different decades.[[178]](#cite_note-178)

Despite the nature of his departure from the Bills and having a losing record with Buffalo, Fitzpatrick and [Bills Mafia](/wiki/Bills_Mafia "Bills Mafia") continue to hold each other in high esteem. Upon his retirement, Fitzpatrick listed Buffalo as his "favorite place to play."[[51]](#cite_note-Sullivan_on_Fitz_retirement-51)

> "I don't know that I've ever felt more at home in a stadium or with a fanbase. I was in Buffalo for four years, but those are my people. I feel like I understand them and they understand me, and it was one of the great pleasures of my career playing there."

— Ryan Fitzpatrick reflecting on his time in Buffalo on [Adam Schefter](/wiki/Adam_Schefter "Adam Schefter")'s podcast[[52]](#cite_note-52)

*[Sports Illustrated](/wiki/Sports_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")* comments that Fitzpatrick remains a fan favorite in Buffalo due to the manner in which he connected with the fandom and integrated himself and his family with the Buffalo community during his time on the Bills.[[53]](#cite_note-SI_retirement-53) Journalist Jerry Sullivan also notes that Fitzpatrick's resilience and passion endeared him to fans and that his tenure on the Bills cemented his playing style as a gunslinger.[[51]](#cite_note-Sullivan_on_Fitz_retirement-51)

The 1911 statute stated:

> The bear flag is hereby selected and adopted as the state flag of California. ... The said bear flag shall consist of a flag of a length equal to one and one-half the width thereof; the upper five-sixths of the width thereof to be a white field, and the lower sixth of the width thereof to be a red stripe; there shall appear in the white field in the upper left-hand corner a single [red star](/wiki/Red_star "Red star"), and at the bottom of the white field the words '[California Republic](/wiki/California_Republic "California Republic"),' and in the center of the white field a California grizzly bear upon a grass plat, in the position of walking toward the left of the said field; said bear shall be dark brown in color and in length, equal to one-third of the length of said flag.

In 1953, the design and specifications for the state flag were standardized in a bill signed by Governor [Earl Warren](/wiki/Earl_Warren "Earl Warren") and illustrated by Donald Graeme Kelley of Marin County, California.[[5]](#cite_note-5) The Californian state flag is often called the "Bear Flag" and in fact, the present statute adopting the flag, [California Government Code § 420](http://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=420&lawCode=GOV), states: "The Bear Flag is the State Flag of California."

In late 2023, talks of a possible joint ticket between the KMT and TPP began.[[59]](#cite_note-59) It was initially unclear if the KMT's [Hou Yu-ih](/wiki/Hou_Yu-ih "Hou Yu-ih") and the TPP's [Ko Wen-je](/wiki/Ko_Wen-je "Ko Wen-je") would join as a ticket, let alone who would be the nominee for president and vice president once a joint ticket was announced.[[49]](#cite_note-auto1-49) The DPP's Lai stated he would be able to take on the challenge of a joint ticket, and criticized the coalition plans, arguing the two parties do not share enough similarity in ideology.[[60]](#cite_note-60) In November, Ko said that deciding who would lead the ticket as the presidential nominee was the 'only hurdle' remaining in forming the ticket.[[49]](#cite_note-auto1-49) On 13 November, the KMT and TPP agreed to use polling to determine the composition of the joint presidential ticket.[[61]](#cite_note-:0-61) The order of the joint ticket was to be chosen based on opinion polls and publicly announced on 18 November,[[62]](#cite_note-62) but the two sides were unable to come to an agreement on that date.[[63]](#cite_note-63) On 18 November, the original deal collapsed following a dispute regarding the polling.[[64]](#cite_note-64) The KMT and TPP were reportedly unable to come to a consensus surrounding the margins of error.[[65]](#cite_note-65) Despite the initial collapse, there were still attempts to form a coalition ticket. FIFA World Cup :: Results :: part 04 :: chunk_0019
In all, 80 nations have [played in at least one World Cup](/wiki/National_team_appearances_in_the_FIFA_World_Cup "National team appearances in the FIFA World Cup").[[n 4]](#cite_note-successor-117) Of these, eight national teams have won the World Cup,[[114]](#cite_note-118) and they have added [stars to their badges](/wiki/Star_(football_badge) "Star (football badge)"), with each star representing a World Cup victory. Uruguay, however, chose to display [four stars on their badge](/wiki/Four_stars_above_Uruguay%27s_football_crest "Four stars above Uruguay's football crest"), representing their two gold medals at the 1924 and 1928 Summer Olympics, which are recognized by FIFA as World Championships, and their two World Cup titles in 1930 and 1950.

With five titles, Brazil are the most successful World Cup team and also the only nation to have [played in every World Cup](/wiki/National_team_appearances_in_the_FIFA_World_Cup#Finals_records_by_team "National team appearances in the FIFA World Cup") (22) to date.[[115]](#cite_note-119) Brazil were also the first team to win the World Cup for the third (1970), fourth (1994) and fifth (2002) time. Italy (1934 and 1938) and Brazil (1958 and 1962) are the only nations to have won consecutive titles. West Germany (1982–1990) and Brazil (1994–2002) are the only nations to appear in three consecutive World Cup finals. Germany has made the most top-four finishes (13), medals (12), as well as the most finals (8).
